core.name: Emporia
core.why: Malmö's largest shopping centre at Hyllie, one of the biggest in Scandinavia, with a striking facade by Wingårdh.
evidence: sources: wikivoyage buy, visitmalmo, wikivoyage-sv, wikipedia

core.name: Triangeln
core.why: The largest shopping centre in central Malmö, built over Triangeln station; 'vid Triangeln' is everyday Malmö orientation.

core.name: Mobilia
core.why: Large shopping centre with over a hundred shops at Dalaplan/Per Albins väg, in the old Malmö Yllefabrik buildings.
evidence: sources: wikivoyage buy, visitmalmo, wikivoyage-sv, wikipedia

core.name: Hansa
core.why: City-centre galleria between Stora Nygatan and Södra Promenaden, the former NK building, still universally called Hansa.

core.name: Malmö Saluhall
core.why: The city's food hall in an old goods warehouse by Centralstationen, opened 2016.
evidence: sources: whiteguide REKOMMENDERAD, wikivoyage eat, visitmalmo äta

core.name: Möllevångstorget
core.why: Malmö's market square, with daily stall trade in fruit and vegetables since the early 1900s.

core.name: Åhléns City
core.why: The department store on Södergatan by Gustav Adolfs torg, a classic meeting point ('vid Åhléns').
evidence: OSM shop=department_store, branch=city (dropped from long list as a chain)

core.name: Jägersro Center
core.why: Long-standing shopping centre from 1962 opposite Jägersro racecourse, staying as the new Jägersro district is built around it.

core.name: Svågertorp
core.why: The big-box retail area by the bridge approach with IKEA and many others; 'Svågertorp' is the name residents use for it.

core.name: Kv. Caroli
core.why: The Caroli block in the old town (Caroli City), still widely known by name even though it is now more offices and homes than mall.

core.name: Burlöv Center
core.why: Shopping centre in Arlöv just outside the city line, opened 1971 and widely used by Malmö residents in the north-east.

core.name: Rosengård Centrum
core.why: The centre and square of Rosengård, a well-known name and bus stop across the city.

core.name: Kronprinsen
core.why: The 1964 skyscraper with a shopping centre at its base on Regementsgatan; a top direction-giving landmark in the west of the city.

missing.name: IKEA Malmö
missing.why: Huge blue box at Svågertorp, seen from the E20/bridge approach; residents use it as a reference point. Dropped from the long list as a brand.

missing.name: Södergatan
missing.why: Malmö's first pedestrian street (1978), the main shopping street between Stortorget and Gustav Adolfs torg ('gågatan'). Ways 28411524, 1123355063, 189255275, 1360214423.

notes: Hansa: the game calls it Hansacompagniet, but since the post-2017 rebuild it is called just Hansa, and residents say Hansa; consider renaming. Kronprinsen is mainly a skyscraper, so if a buildings category claims it, drop it here. Kv. Caroli overlaps with Caroli kyrka in the game. Svågertorp vs IKEA: I made the area core and IKEA not core; flip them if a single-building target suits the quiz better. Södergatan is a street and probably belongs to the street questions, but it is the shopping street. Entré (2009, Fredsgatan/Värnhem) has been in decline and has been rebuilt several times; it is still open but not core. Cantin is a seasonal street-food park in Varvsstaden (April to September, first season 2026), too new for core. Marknadsbörsen (Fricksgatan 4, near Möllan) is a weekend market with little public profile, so it is borderline. Malmö has no NK. Lagerhuset and Dalaplan as shopping places: there is no Lagerhuset in OSM, and Dalaplan is a square whose shopping is Mobilia. Malmö Designer Village is in Löddeköpinge (opens 2027), outside the area. Väla is outside the bbox.
